newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGB futures end down after paring earlier gains.
newsitem.headline: JGB futures end down after paring earlier gains.

text.p: The key September 10-year Japanese government bond futures contract ended slightly lower on Monday due to hedge selling by dealers, traders said.
"There was talk that a city bank had sold 10-year JGBs, and that dealers who bought the bonds from them sold JGB futures for hedging purposes," a brokerage house trader said.
In the cash bond market, talk that the Finance Ministry is likely to cut the volume of six-year JGBs to be offered through an auction on Tuesday helped boost medium-term JGBs, traders said.
The September ended at 124.10, down slightly from Friday's close of 124.15.
The benchmark 182nd 10-year JGB yield stood at 2.370 percent as of 0636 GMT, unchanged from Friday's close.
Traders said JGBs pared earlier gains in the afternoon as sentiment was weakened by large-lot selling of the September which took place early in the afternoon session.
"About 30 billion yen worth of the September was sold at around 124.18," a trader for a trust bank's securities unit said.
JGBs were firm earlier, supported by a fall in interest rate swap (IRS) rates, traders said.
A long-term credit bank as well as some city banks were detected receiving fixed interest rates, especially in the three- and four-year zones in the morning session, they said.
"The market now feels the Bank of Japan is unlikely to change its monetary policy for the time being," the brokerage house trader said.
Traders expect MOF to cut the amount of six-year JGBs it offers through an auction on Tuesday to 400 billion yen from 500 billion yen at the previous auction.
The traders said MOF showed that it intended to reduce the volume of six-year JGBs offered when it consulted market participants on Monday morning about demand for new bonds.
When the MOF last auctioned six-year bonds on May 8, it offered 500 billion yen worth at a coupon rate of 1.8 percent.
Medium-term JGBs were bought once talk of the expected reduction became widespread, the brokerage house trader said.
"The 20th six-year JGB was sold initially, but bought back later due to the talk," he said.
